interactions are probably the result of an overlap of mineral

Minerals are transported in blood bound to protein carriers. 
The protein binding is either specific (e.g., transferrin, which 
binds with iron, or ceruloplasmin, which binds with copper) or 
general (e.g., albumin, which binds with a variety of minerals). 
A fraction of each mineral also is carried in the serum as amino 
acid or peptide complexes. Specific protein carriers are usually 
not completely saturated; the reserve capacity may serve as a 
buffer against excessive exposure. Toxicity from minerals usu-
ally results only after this buffering capacity is exceeded.
